1.s: Jesus’s family tree from Abraham through David, then his birth: an angel tells Joseph that Mary’s child is from the Holy Spirit, to be named Jesus, “for it is he who shall save his people from their sins.”
1.d: The family line is set out in three sets of fourteen generations [[bible:Matthew 1:17]]; fourteen may point to David, since the letters of his Hebrew name add up to fourteen [[tosn:Matthew 1:17]]. It names women too, some from outside Israel such as Rahab, a sign of God’s grace [[tosn:Matthew 1:5]] [[bsn:Matthew 1:1-17]]. Matthew quotes Isaiah 7:14: Immanuel, “God with us” [[tosn:Matthew 1:22-23]] [[bible:Matthew 1:23]].

2.s: Wise men from the east follow a star to worship the child in Bethlehem. King Herod tries to kill him; the family flees to Egypt, and later settles in Nazareth.
2.d: Jesus relives Israel’s story: as God once called Israel out of Egypt, so he calls his Son (Hosea 11:1) [[tosn:Matthew 2:15]]. Bethlehem mattered because King David was born there [[tosn:Matthew 2:6]]. Herod the Great reigned until 4 BC [[tbd:008:Herod, Herodian Family]], so Jesus was born a little before that.

3.s: John the Baptizer preaches in the wilderness: “Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand!” Jesus is baptized, the Spirit descends like a dove, and a voice says, “This is my beloved Son.”
3.d: At Jesus’ baptism God made himself known as the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit [[bsn:Matthew 3:13-17]]. The Father’s words echo Psalm 2:7 and Isaiah 42:1 [[tosn:Matthew 3:17]].

4.s: Jesus is tempted in the wilderness for forty days and answers the devil with Scripture. He begins preaching in Galilee and calls fishermen: “Come after me, and I will make you fishers for men.”
4.d: Jesus answered each temptation with words from Deuteronomy [[bsn:Matthew 4:1-11]]. His forty days recall Israel’s forty years of testing in the wilderness [[tosn:Matthew 4:2]].

5.s: The Sermon on the Mount begins: the Beatitudes (“Blessed are the poor in spirit”), salt and light, and Jesus’s teaching that goes beyond the law: anger, lust, oaths, revenge, and “Love your enemies.”
5.d: Jesus came not to destroy the law or the prophets, but to fulfil them [[bible:Matthew 5:17]]. Six times he says “You have heard… But I tell you”, correcting misunderstandings of the law [[tosn:Matthew 5:21-47]] with an authority all his own [[tosn:Matthew 7:28-29]].

6.s: Give, pray and fast in secret, not for show. The Lord’s Prayer. Store up treasure in heaven. “Don’t be anxious… seek first God’s Kingdom.”
6.d: The Lord’s Prayer is a simple pattern for prayer [[tosn:Matthew 6:7-8]], and Jesus calls God “Father”, which most Jewish prayers did not do [[tosn:Matthew 6:9]]. The closing praise, “For yours is the Kingdom…”, is missing from some manuscripts and was probably drawn from 1 Chronicles 29:11–13 [[tosn:Matthew 6:13]] [[webfn:Matthew 6:13]].

7.s: Don’t judge. Ask, seek, knock. The Golden Rule. The narrow gate. A tree is known by its fruit. The wise man builds his house on the rock.
7.d: The teachers of the law leaned on Scripture and on earlier scholars, but Jesus taught with his own authority [[tosn:Matthew 7:28-29]]. Those who hear his words and do them are like the wise builder [[bsn:Matthew 7:24-29]].

8.s: Jesus heals a leper, a centurion’s servant and Peter’s mother-in-law, calms a storm, and frees two men from demons.
8.d: The centurion’s faith shows that God’s kingdom includes people from every nation [[tosn:Matthew 8:8-10]], as God promised Abraham [[tosn:Matthew 8:11-12]]. A centurion commanded about a hundred Roman soldiers [[tosn:Matthew 8:5]].

9.s: Jesus heals a paralysed man and forgives his sins, calls Matthew the tax collector, raises a girl, and heals a bleeding woman and two blind men. “The harvest indeed is plentiful, but the laborers are few.”
9.d: Jesus quotes Hosea 6:6, “I desire mercy, and not sacrifice” [[bible:Matthew 9:13]], and shows that mercy by eating with sinners [[tosn:Matthew 9:13]].

10.s: Jesus sends out the twelve apostles to preach and heal, warning of persecution: “Don’t be afraid… you are of more value than many sparrows.”
10.d: This is the second of Jesus’ long teachings in Matthew [[bsn:Matthew 10:1-15]]. Even a cup of cold water given to a disciple will be rewarded [[bible:Matthew 10:42]].

11.s: John the Baptist in prison asks if Jesus is the one; Jesus points to his works. “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.”
11.d: John is the Elijah who was to come, as Malachi promised [[tosn:Matthew 11:14-15]] [[bible:Malachi 4:5]]. Jesus invites those weighed down by burdensome rules to come to him and find rest [[tosn:Matthew 11:29-30]].

12.s: Conflicts over the Sabbath. The Pharisees say Jesus casts out demons by Beelzebul. Jesus speaks of the sign of Jonah and of his true family.
12.d: Matthew shows Jesus fulfilling Isaiah’s words about God’s gentle servant [[bsn:Matthew 12:15-21]]. Jesus is greater than the temple, greater than Jonah and greater than Solomon [[tosn:Matthew 12:41-42]].

13.s: Parables of the Kingdom: the sower, the weeds, the mustard seed, the yeast, the hidden treasure, the pearl and the net. Jesus is rejected in Nazareth.
13.d: The third of Jesus’ long teachings, full of parables about God’s kingdom [[tosn:Matthew 13:1-53]] [[bsn:Matthew 13:1-23]]. Finding the kingdom brings more joy than any passing pleasure [[tosn:Matthew 13:44]].

14.s: Herod beheads John the Baptist. Jesus feeds five thousand, walks on the water, and Peter steps out of the boat, then sinks.
14.d: Walking on the water shows Jesus’ power over nature, and the disciples worship him as the Son of God [[tosn:Matthew 14:22-33]].

15.s: Jesus teaches that what defiles comes from the heart. A Canaanite woman’s great faith; healings; the feeding of four thousand.
15.d: Jesus’ silence tested the woman’s faith [[tosn:Matthew 15:23]]. She calls him “Son of David”, as if she understood that he was the Messiah [[tosn:Matthew 15:22]], and her humble, persistent reply wins his praise [[bsn:Matthew 15:21-28]].

16.s: Peter confesses, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” Jesus says he will build his church on this rock, then foretells his death and calls followers to take up their cross.
16.d: Peter’s name, Petros, means “rock”, and Jesus plays on it: “on this rock” (petra) [[tosn:Matthew 16:18]]. Christians have long differed on whether the rock is Peter himself, his confession of faith, or Christ [[tosn:Matthew 16:18]]. Peter’s confession shows that God had opened his eyes [[tosn:Matthew 16:16]].

17.s: Jesus is transfigured on a mountain with Moses and Elijah. He heals a boy and pays the temple tax with a coin from a fish’s mouth.
17.d: Even faith as small as a mustard seed can do great things [[tosn:Matthew 17:20]] [[bible:Matthew 17:20]].

18.s: Who is greatest? Become like a child. The lost sheep; how to correct a brother; forgive “seventy times seven”; the parable of the unforgiving servant.
18.d: The fourth of Jesus’ long teachings, on life together in the community of disciples: humility, care for the lost, correcting and restoring one another, and forgiving [[tosn:Matthew 18:1-35]] [[tosn:Matthew 18:18-20]].

19.s: Teaching on marriage and divorce; Jesus blesses children; a rich young man goes away sad. “With God all things are possible.”
19.d: Marriage is meant to last for life [[tosn:Matthew 19:9]]. The rich man’s refusal to follow Jesus showed that his wealth came before God [[tosn:Matthew 19:21-22]]. “But many will be last who are first” [[bible:Matthew 19:30]].

20.s: The parable of the workers in the vineyard, paid the same. Jesus foretells his death again, teaches that the greatest must serve, and heals two blind men.
20.d: Jesus’ followers serve others, as he did [[tosn:Matthew 20:27]]: the Son of Man came to serve and to give his life as a ransom, a payment freely given to rescue many [[tosn:Matthew 20:28]] [[bible:Matthew 20:28]].

21.s: Jesus enters Jerusalem on a donkey to cries of “Hosanna to the son of David!”, clears the temple, curses a fig tree, and tells parables of two sons and the wicked tenants.
21.d: For the first time Jesus openly acts as Israel’s King and Messiah [[bsn:Matthew 21:1-17]], riding a donkey as Zechariah 9:9 foretold, a sign of his humble, peaceful rule [[tosn:Matthew 21:4-5]]. The rejected stone becoming the cornerstone (Psalm 118) speaks of Jesus himself [[tosn:Matthew 21:42]].

22.s: The parable of the wedding feast. Questions about taxes, the resurrection and the greatest commandment. Whose son is the Christ?
22.d: Love God, and love your neighbour as yourself (Leviticus 19:18) [[tosn:Matthew 22:39]]: “The whole law and the prophets depend on these two commandments” [[bible:Matthew 22:40]].

23.s: Seven woes against the scribes and Pharisees for hypocrisy. Jesus laments over Jerusalem: “How often I would have gathered your children together, even as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings”
23.d: Jesus’ words of judgement are aimed at a group of Israel’s leaders who taught with authority but did not care for the people [[bsn:Matthew 23:1-39]]. Some Christians later misused such passages against Jewish people [[tosn:Matthew 27:25]].

24.s: On the Mount of Olives Jesus foretells the temple’s destruction, wars and persecution, and the coming of the Son of Man. “Watch.”
24.d: Chapters 23–25 are the last of Jesus’ long teachings, on judgement [[tosn:Matthew 23:1-25:46]]. Scholars differ on which sayings point to the fall of Jerusalem in AD 70 and which to Christ’s return [[tosn:Matthew 10:23]] [[tosn:Matthew 24:30]].

25.s: Parables of the ten bridesmaids and the talents, and the judgement of the nations: “because you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.”
25.d: When believers care for the hungry, strangers, the sick and prisoners, they are serving Jesus himself [[bsn:Matthew 25:31-46]], and the duty to care reaches to everyone in need [[tosn:Matthew 25:40]].

26.s: A woman anoints Jesus; Judas agrees to betray him for thirty pieces of silver. At the Last Supper Jesus gives bread and wine. He prays in Gethsemane, “not what I desire, but what you desire” is arrested, tried, and Peter denies him.
26.d: At the Passover meal Jesus gives his blood as the blood of the new covenant promised in Jeremiah 31:31 [[tosn:Matthew 26:28]] [[bsn:Matthew 26:17-30]]: “This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the remission of sins” [[bible:Matthew 26:28]].

27.s: Judas hangs himself. Pilate washes his hands and hands Jesus over. He is crucified; darkness falls; the curtain tears; the earth shakes. Joseph of Arimathea buries him, and the tomb is guarded.
27.d: Pilate washes his hands, likely because he did not believe Jesus guilty of rebellion against Rome [[tosn:Matthew 27:58]] [[bible:Matthew 27:24]]. The cry “May his blood be on us, and on our children!” has been misunderstood and misused by some Christians to persecute Jews [[tosn:Matthew 27:25]].

28.s: On the first day of the week the women find the stone rolled away; the risen Jesus meets them. In Galilee he tells the eleven: “Go and make disciples of all nations… I am with you always, even to the end of the age.”
28.d: The mission to all nations begins here, and baptism marks a person as belonging to Jesus [[tosn:Matthew 28:19]]. The Gospel ends as it began, with God with us [[bsn:Matthew 28:16-20]] [[bible:Matthew 1:23]] [[bible:Matthew 28:20]].
